events.title: Bruneian Sultanate Established
events.description: Brunei established an Islamic sultanate, becoming a powerful maritime trading state in northern Borneo. Brunei controlled northern Borneo and parts of southern Philippines.

events.title: Bruneian Empire at Its Peak
events.description: The Bruneian Sultanate reached its zenith, with territory including all of northern Borneo and southwestern Philippines (including present-day Manila). Brunei became an important trade and Islamic cultural center in Southeast Asia.

events.title: Oil Discovered
events.description: A major oil field was discovered in Seria, Brunei, beginning commercial oil production. Oil changed Brunei's destiny, bringing enormous wealth to the small nation.

events.title: Brunei People's Party Rebellion
events.description: The left-wing Brunei People's Party launched an armed rebellion, demanding to join Malaysia and implement democracy. British forces swiftly suppressed the rebellion. Sultan Omar used this as a pretext to ban political parties and implement authoritarian rule.

events.title: Hassanal Bolkiah Ascends Throne
events.description: 29-year-old Prince Hassanal Bolkiah became the 29th Sultan, succeeding his abdicated father. He has ruled Brunei to this day, becoming one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs.

events.title: Brunei Independence
events.description: Brunei gained independence from British protection, becoming a sovereign nation. Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah became head of state and prime minister. January 1 became Brunei's National Day.

events.title: Full Implementation of Islamic Criminal Law
events.description: Brunei announced full implementation of Sharia law, including capital punishment such as stoning for homosexuality. International strong protests and UN condemnation followed. Under pressure, the Sultan announced a moratorium on executing death penalty provisions.

events.title: Early Civilization
events.description: Early Malay civilization emerged in Brunei region, trading with China and India. Chinese historical records mention 'Poni' (ancient name for Brunei) paying tribute to China.

events.title: Sultan Visits China
events.description: Bruneian Sultan twice visited Ming Dynasty China, establishing tributary relations. The first Sultan died during his visit to Nanjing, and Emperor Yongle held a grand funeral for him.

events.title: Magellan Reaches Brunei
events.description: Portuguese explorer Magellan's fleet reached Brunei, marking first European contact. The West began learning about this wealthy Southeast Asian sultanate.

events.title: Spanish Invasion
events.description: Spain invaded Brunei from Philippines, occupying the capital. However, Spain quickly withdrew due to disease and supply difficulties. This invasion began weakening Brunei's power.

events.title: Bruneian Decline
events.description: Bruneian Empire gradually declined, losing vast territories. Civil wars, succession disputes, and piracy activities weakened the state. Sulu Sultanate of Philippines and White Rajah regime in Sarawak encroached on Bruneian territory.

events.title: Brooke Family Occupies Sarawak
events.description: British adventurer James Brooke assisted Bruneian Sultan in suppressing rebellion, receiving Sarawak region and establishing 'White Rajah Kingdom.' Brunei lost extensive territory.

events.title: Continued Territory Loss
events.description: Brunei ceded more territory to Brooke family and British North Borneo Company. Bruneian territory shrank from all of Borneo to today's small nation.

events.title: British Protectorate
events.description: Brunei became British protectorate, with Britain controlling foreign affairs and defense. Sultan retained internal autonomy. This saved Brunei from complete annexation.

events.title: British Resident in Brunei
events.description: Britain appointed Resident to Brunei, effectively controlling internal affairs. Sultan became puppet ruler.

events.title: Japanese Occupation
events.description: During WWII Japan occupied Brunei, extensively plundering oil resources. After Japan's surrender, Australian forces liberated Brunei, and British rule was restored.

events.title: Constitution Promulgated
events.description: Brunei promulgated constitution, establishing Legislative Council, implementing partial autonomy. However, Britain still controlled foreign affairs and defense.

events.title: Refused to Join Malaysia
events.description: When Malaysia was formed, Bruneian Sultan refused to join (reasons included oil revenue distribution and sultan status issues). Brunei continued as British protectorate.

events.title: British Withdrawal from East of Suez
events.description: Britain announced withdrawal from regions east of Suez. Brunei began negotiating independence with Britain.

events.title: Joined UN and ASEAN
events.description: Brunei joined United Nations and Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), integrating into international community and regional cooperation.

events.title: 'Malay Islamic Monarchy' Ideology
events.description: Brunei established 'Malay Islamic Monarchy' (Melayu Islam Beraja, MIB) as national ideology, emphasizing trinity of Malay culture, Islam, and monarchy.

events.title: Legislative Council Restored
events.description: Brunei restored Legislative Council after 40-year hiatus, but all members appointed by Sultan. Brunei remains absolute monarchy.

events.title: Implementation of Islamic Criminal Law
events.description: Brunei began phased implementation of strict Sharia law, drawing international criticism. Law includes severe punishments for homosexuality and adultery.

events.title: Oil Dependency and Economic Diversification
events.description: Brunei is one of world's wealthiest countries with extremely high per capita GDP, citizens enjoying free education and healthcare. However, economy highly dependent on oil and gas (over 60% of GDP), facing energy transition challenges. Government promoting economic diversification, but progress slow.

events.title: Sultan's 55th Year on Throne
events.description: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah has reigned for 55 years, world's second-longest reigning monarch (after late Queen Elizabeth II). He combines roles of Sultan, Prime Minister, Defense Minister, and Finance Minister, wielding absolute power.

events.title: Crown Prince Succession Preparation
events.description: Crown Prince Al-Muhtadee Billah gradually assumes more responsibilities, preparing for future succession. Bruneian royal family wealth estimated at $28 billion, one of world's wealthiest royal families.
